facts.statement: More than 100 fossil and subfossil individuals of Teratornis have been found across California, Oregon, Nevada, Arizona, and Florida, with the majority coming from the La Brea Tar Pits.
facts.quote: A large number of fossil and subfossil bones, representing more than 100 individuals, have been found in locations in California, Oregon, southern Nevada, Arizona, and Florida, though most are from the Californian La Brea Tar Pits.

facts.statement: All known Teratornis remains date to the Late Pleistocene, except for one partial Early Pleistocene skeleton found in Florida.
facts.quote: All remains are known from the Late Pleistocene except one partial skeleton from the Early Pleistocene Leisey Shell Pit near Charlotte Harbor, Florida.

facts.statement: The species Teratornis woodburnensis was discovered in 1999 at Legion Park in Woodburn, Oregon, north of the La Brea Tar Pits.
facts.quote: The first species to be found north of the La Brea Tar Pits, this partial specimen was discovered at Legion Park, Woodburn, Oregon in 1999.

facts.statement: Teratornis merriami stood approximately 75 cm tall with an estimated wingspan of 3.5 to 3.8 meters and a weight between 12.5 and 15.0 kg.
facts.quote: It stood about 75 cm (29.5 in) tall with estimated wingspan of perhaps 3.5 to 3.8 metres (11.5 to 12.5 ft), and its weight has been estimated within the range of 12.5 - 15.0 kg with 95% confidence

facts.statement: Teratornis merriami went extinct at the end of the Pleistocene, approximately 10,000 years ago.
facts.quote: It became extinct at the very end of the Pleistocene, some 10,000 years ago.

facts.statement: The partial skeleton of Teratornis woodburnensis indicates an estimated wingspan of over 4 meters.
facts.quote: It is known from a humerus, parts of the cranium, beak, sternum, and vertebrae which indicate an estimated wingspan of over 4 meters (14 ft).

facts.statement: A 1945 description estimated Teratornis merriami had a wingspan of 3.5 to 3.8 meters, a wing area of 17.5 square meters, and a height of 75 cm.
facts.quote: According to description of 1945, Teratornis merriami had a wingspan of around 3.5 to 3.8 m and a wing area of 17.5 square meters, standing an estimated 75 cm tall.

facts.statement: Calculations based on the sternum and synsacrum estimated Teratornis merriami weighed about 22.5 kg, nearly double the weight of an average California condor.
facts.quote: by calculating the area of the organism's sternum and synsacrum, Teratornis was estimated to weigh about 22.5 kg, which was nearly double the weight of an average Californian condor.

facts.statement: A 1983 study estimated a wingspan range of 2.938 to 3.379 meters and a weight of 13.7 kg for Teratornis merriami.
facts.quote: A 1983 study gives a range of wingspan of 2.938 – 3.379 m and a weight of 13.7 kg.

facts.statement: Teratornis had fused finger bones with a specialized shelf on the index finger that helped support long primary feathers for utilizing strong upcurrents in flight.
facts.quote: The finger bones of Teratornis were fused as in all modern birds; however, part of the index finger forms a shelf which aided in bearing the load of long and stout primaries, enabling the bird to utilize strong upcurrents in flight.

facts.statement: Teratornis likely primarily inhabited cliff terrain to facilitate takeoff and soaring flight.
facts.quote: Thus, Teratornis may have primarily inhabited cliff terrain, where it could take off and soar through the air easily.

facts.statement: Analysis of skull morphology suggests Teratornis merriami was an active predator capable of swallowing prey whole, rather than just a scavenger.
facts.quote: Teratornis merriami was similar to condors, although an analysis of the functional morphology of its skull, namely its larger beak and ability to spread its mandibles and swallow its prey whole, suggests that it was an active predator rather than a scavenger.

facts.statement: Teratornis merriami likely swallowed small prey like frogs and lizards whole and fed on carrion similarly to condors or vultures.
facts.quote: For T. merriami, small prey such as frogs, lizards, young birds, and small mammals were swallowed whole, while carrion would have been fed on in a manner similar to that of condors or vultures.

facts.statement: Teratornis could maintain flight in changing air currents due to emarginated primary feathers that separate and move independently.
facts.quote: Their ability to react to these changes and maintain flight has to do with their emarginated primary feathers which separate and move independently during flight, contrary to the unemarginated primary feathers of birds who dynamically soar on more reliable air currents.

facts.statement: Teratorns are thought to have been attracted to the La Brea Tar Pits by megafauna trapped in asphalt, leading the teratorns to fall victim to the sticky deposits themselves.
facts.quote: Teratorns are thought to have been attracted by Pleistocene megafauna that became stuck and died in the viscous asphalt while trying to drink from pools of water that gathered on the surface, with the teratorns subsequently falling victim to the sticky deposits.

facts.statement: The families Teratornithidae, Vulturidae, and Ciconiidae can be differentiated by skull morphology related to different feeding methods.
facts.quote: Despite similarities, these three families can be differentiated by their differing skulls in response to significantly different feeding methods.

facts.statement: The genus Aiolornis was formerly known as Teratornis incredibilis but is now considered distinct enough to be its own genus.
facts.quote: A closely related genus, Aiolornis, was about 40% larger and lived at an earlier time; it was formerly known as Teratornis incredibilis, but is distinct enough to be placed in its own genus.

facts.statement: The genus Teratornis was described by L. H. Miller in 1909.
facts.quote: genus_authority: L. H. Miller, 1909

facts.statement: Teratornis belongs to the extinct family Teratornithidae.
facts.quote: familia: Teratornithidae †

facts.statement: Most Teratornis remains date to the Lower Pleistocene, with one partial skeleton from Florida dating to the Upper Pleistocene, and the most recent fossils dating to the Pleistocene-Holocene boundary.
facts.quote: Todos los restos datan del Pleistoceno Inferior, pero un esqueleto parcial proveniente de Leisey Shell, cerca de Charlotte Harbor, Florida (que puede representar una especie o subespecie) datan del Pleistoceno superior, y los más recientes datan de la división entre el Pleistoceno y el Holoceno.

facts.statement: Teratornis had fused toe bones like modern birds, but part of the index toe formed a platform that increased its wing loading.
facts.quote: Los huesos de los dedos están fusionados como en todas las aves modernas, sin embargo, parte del dedo índice forma una plataforma que aumenta su carga alar

facts.statement: Its legs were similar to those of an Andean condor but more robust, and its claws could have been used to tear pieces from prey.
facts.quote: Las patas eran similares a las un cóndor andino, pero más robustas, y las garras podrían haberse utilizado para arrancar pedazos a sus presas

facts.statement: Teratornis merriami had a wing loading not much greater than a California condor and could likely take off by jumping and flapping a little.
facts.quote: Su carga alar no era mucho mayor que la de un cóndor de California, y Teratornis merriami debía haber sido capaz de despegar con sólo saltar y aletear un poco

facts.statement: The small size of its legs suggests it was better adapted to take off from elevated places like California condors.
facts.quote: como lo demuestra el poco tamaño de sus patas

facts.statement: Teratornis merriami likely swallowed small prey the size of rabbits in one bite and consumed carrion similarly to vultures and condors.
facts.quote: Probablemente ingería presas pequeñas del tamaño de conejos de un solo bocado, mientras que la carroña era consumida de una manera similar a la de buitres y cóndores

facts.statement: Analyses of its skull and beak suggest that fish were an important part of its diet.
facts.quote: diversos análisis de su cráneo y pico sugieren que los peces eran parte importante de su dieta

facts.statement: It is very possible that Teratornis hunted aquatic prey in a manner similar to fish eagles.
facts.quote: es muy posible que se diera a la caza de presas acuáticas de forma similar a las águilas pescadoras

facts.statement: Teratornis merriami lived similarly to modern condors, but its larger beak suggests it was a more active predator.
facts.quote: Los teratornis de Merriam vivían de manera similar a la de los cóndores actuales, aunque el mayor tamaño de su pico sugiere que se trataba de un depredador más activo

facts.statement: Many bones found in the La Brea Tar Pits are attributed to Teratornis individuals attracted to Pleistocene megafauna water pools on the tar surface.
facts.quote: El gran número de huesos encontrados en La Brea Tar Pits suelen ser considerados como de Teratornis que fueron atraídos como la gran mayoría de la megafauna del Pleistoceno: tratando de beber de los charcos de agua que se formaban en la superficie de la brea

facts.statement: The genus Teratornis lived from the Calabrian to the Holocene, spanning 1.8 to 0 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Calabrian to Holocene (1.8 to 0 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Teratornis belongs to the parent group Teratornithidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Teratornithidae

facts.statement: Teratornis is classified within the family Teratornithidae.
facts.quote: Family: Teratornithidae

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Teratornis is Teratornis merriami.
facts.quote: Type species: Teratornis merriami

facts.statement: Teratornis merriami was the largest flying bird encountered by humans in its lifetime.
facts.quote: T. merriami fue la mayor ave voladora que se haya encontrado en vida con el hombre

facts.statement: The species was large enough and possibly aggressive enough to attempt feeding on human infants, though not regularly.
facts.quote: la especie fue lo suficientemente grande y, posiblemente, lo suficientemente abusiva como para tratar de alimentarse de bebés humanos

facts.statement: It is debated whether the memory of Teratornis persisted enough to form the basis of thunderbird myths.
facts.quote: tal vez su memoria persistió lo suficiente como para ser la base de los mitos de los thunderbirds (aves del trueno)

facts.statement: Recent isotopic studies suggest the California condor survived megafauna extinction by consuming dead marine mammals off the Pacific coast.
facts.quote: Estudios isotópicos recientes sugieren que el cóndor de California ha logrado sobrevivir a la extinción de la megafauna, ya que también llega a consumir mamíferos marinos muertos frente a la costa del Pacífico
